claims.author: ismaelsadeeq
claims.question: whether collectTxs() can return missing transaction positions directly to reduce an IPC round trip
claims.quote: This could be collapsed to the response "JDS calls TxCollection::collectTxs() (this PR) with that Wtxid list" to reduce the round trip?

status_by.quote: collectTxs() is the constructor so it needs to return an interface. I don't think it can return both the TxCollection interface and the list of missing transactions.

claims.status_note: author explained collectTxs is a constructor returning an interface and pipelining can chain requests

claims.author: ViniciusCestarii
claims.harm: order-dependent addition in addMissingTxs could leave partially applied state if an invalid transaction aborts the loop early
claims.quote: AddMissingTxs is order-dependent, a bad entry aborts the loop at that point, so [valid, invalid] keeps valid but [invalid, valid] doesn't. Is this intentional? Correct me if I am wrong but validate-then-apply seems to be a safer approach.

claims.author: ViniciusCestarii
claims.quote: would it be worth splitting into two capnp interfaces instead of throwing on methods: an ExternalBlockTemplate with just getBlockHeader/getBlock/getCoinbaseMerklePath/submitSolution and BlockTemplate extends(ExternalBlockTemplate)
claims.request: split into two Cap'n Proto interfaces (ExternalBlockTemplate and BlockTemplate) so disallowed methods fail at compile-time rather than throwing at runtime

status_by.quote: The split just removes what's currently unclear to a client consuming the interface (methods that appear callable but are guaranteed to throw). Just my two cents. I'm fine either way

claims.status_note: reviewer stated they are fine either way after author raised concerns about client duplication

claims.author: gmaxwell
claims.harm: non-differential indices allow repeated requests for the same transaction, risking buffer overflow or out-of-memory errors
claims.quote: compact blocks uses a differential index not primarily for efficiency... but so that the wire format is safe by construction against an attack that applies the same large transaction over and over again (e.g. if index 5 is some giant txn, you request 5,5,5,5,5,5...) and overflows a buffer or OOMs an implementation explicitly constructs the block and without having to have expensive duplication che

status_by.quote: the Mining IPC client is expected to run on the same machine, so unknownTxPos() and addMissingTxs() are not designed for bandwidth efficiency. We also (currently) more or less trust the IPC client.

claims.status_note: author explained Mining IPC client trust model and local host assumption

claims.author: pablomartin4btc
claims.quote: Should the size of `wtxids` be checked before the loop (e.g. perhaps using existing constants — `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT`)?
claims.request: check the size of wtxids before looping using MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT

status_by.quote: Added (similar check as in merkleblock.cpp), along with a test.

claims.status_note: author added the limit check in miner.cpp

claims.author: pablomartin4btc
claims.quote: nit: does the `m_mutex` need to be locked in the constructor? — the object isn't shared until after construction returns, so no concurrent access is possible yet.
claims.request: avoid locking m_mutex in TxCollection constructor since the object is not yet shared
claims.status_note: author dropped the mutex lock in the constructor

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: I think the constructor could check for duplicates before locking the mempool? As the duplicate is entirely visible from the input.
claims.request: check for duplicate wtxids in the constructor before locking the mempool

status_by.quote: Done, checking duplicates first without a lock now.

claims.status_note: author added duplicate wtxid check prior to mempool lock

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: since the collection size is known, we could reserve it before acquiring the mempool lock to avoid the reallocating and rehashing while the mempool is locked
claims.request: call reserve on m_transactions before acquiring the mempool lock
claims.status_note: author implemented reserve prior to lock

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: I think an improvement to this test would be adding a test to verify the mempool snapshot behavior. such that it tests that after the collection is constructed with a transaction in the mempool, if the transaction is removed from the mempool it does not report it as missing.
claims.request: add a test verifying that TxCollection retains transactions when they leave the mempool

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: The current documentation here does not mention that all the transactions must be present before calling this so that this does not happen.
claims.request: document that all non-coinbase transactions must already be present in block.vtx before calling the coinbase helper

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: I think a cleaner approach to this helper would be to have it calculate its own height... const int height{pIndexPrev.nHeight + 1}
claims.request: calculate height locally as a const in the coinbase helper instead of modifying BlockAssembler member

status_by.quote: Taken, and made it a const member function.

claims.status_note: author adopted local calculation and made helper const

claims.author: enirox001
claims.quote: Could we limit its scope to checking completeness and copying the ordered m_transactions into a local vector? The references remain valid after the lock is released, so block construction and TestBlockValidity would not need to hold the collection mutex.
claims.request: limit m_mutex scope in MakeTemplate to checking completeness and copying transactions into a local vector

claims.author: enirox001
claims.question: why interruptWait is permitted on external templates when waitNext throws
claims.quote: waitNext is disabled for external templates, but interruptWait is still allowed? Is there a reason for this?

status_by.quote: Good catch, I probably missed this in a rebase (before I opened the PR).

claims.status_note: author acknowledged oversight and disabled interruptWait as well

claims.author: enirox001
claims.harm: addMissingTxs checks transaction count rather than weight, permitting oversized transaction payloads to be stored before block validation
claims.quote: The check here is against the size, but it does not check the weight. So even though it can reject a million tiny transactions, it can accept 16666 large ones... This would be eventually rejected as oversized in makeTemplate when TestBlockValidity is called, but that is a bit too late.

status_by.quote: I don't think we should take over too much work that TestBlockValidity() does for us. Duplicating consensus checks could introduce new bugs.

claims.status_note: author declined duplicating consensus checks done by TestBlockValidity

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.question: why makeTemplate() uses stale-prevblk for ancestor prevhash when TestBlockValidity and checkBlock use inconclusive-not-best-prevblk
claims.quote: makeTemplate() reports an ancestor prevhash as `stale-prevblk`, but `Mining::checkBlock()` reports that same case as `inconclusive-not-best-prevblk`... Was that difference deliberate?

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.quote: The amount case is covered, the witness commitment one isn't, and that's the one that pins which transactions the coinbase commits to. I flipped a bit of the commitment and it gives bad-witness-merkle-match. Would a case next to this one be worth it?
claims.request: add a test case for makeTemplate rejecting a coinbase with a mismatched witness commitment
claims.status_note: author added test for mismatched witness commitment
